study: Wakabayashi et al. 2020, Numbers Plus supplementary preschool math curriculum + PD (HighScope), ECRQ 53:329-342 (IES R305A110483)
eval_evidence: Authored by the HighScope Educational Research Foundation team (Schweinhart et al.) that both developed Numbers Plus and ran the IES efficacy study; the paper notes 'Numbers Plus was developed by HighScope, and training and coaching are offered by HighScope trainers.'
developer_evidence: All training and in-class coaching were delivered by HighScope-certified trainers/coaches; teachers 'were trained and coached by HighScope trainers affiliated with' the developer.
cascade_evidence: Train-the-trainer model: HighScope Early Childhood Specialists ran a 4-day Numbers Plus Training of Trainers; those site/supervisor trainers/coaches then trained and coached the classroom teachers (>=1 extra hop).
counterfactual_evidence: Control = HighScope curriculum alone with no Numbers Plus (delayed-treatment BAU); control teachers were offered Numbers Plus training only after post-data collection.
coaching_evidence: Recurring in-class coaching: coaches planned to visit each classroom about once every two weeks, delivering up to ~20 in-class coaching contacts per classroom across the program year (over-the-shoulder coaching plus debrief).
student_dose_evidence: Numbers Plus is a supplementary math curriculum delivered by the teacher within regular preschool instruction; no tutoring, pull-out, or student-facing software dose added.
maturity_evidence: Outcomes measured at the end of the single program year for teachers newly trained on Numbers Plus; data collected in a different state each year (MI/ME/OH) with fresh first-year cohorts, no prior-implementation maturity wave.
